Working with results

Source: vignettes/working-with-results.Rmd
working-with-results.Rmd
library(CDCLocator)
providers <- cdc_providers("20176", radius = 10)
tidy <- cdc_providers_tidy(providers)

This article describes what cdc_providers() and cdc_providers_tidy() return, and how to sort, de-duplicate, map and save the results.

What cdc_providers() returns

A tibble with one row per provider record (or, for several ZIP codes with distinct = FALSE, one row per record and ZIP code that found it) and four columns:

Column Contents
type The record type, such as "provider"
id The API’s identifier for the record
search_zipcode The ZIP code whose search found the record
attributes Everything else, nested: name, address, contact details, languages, coordinates and distance

The nested form keeps exactly what the API sent. For most work, pass it to cdc_providers_tidy().

When nothing matches, the result has these four columns and zero rows.

What cdc_providers_tidy() returns

One row for each row of the cdc_providers() result, with these columns:

Column Contents
provider_type The record type (from type)
provider_id The API’s identifier (from id)
search_zipcode The ZIP code whose search found the record. With several ZIP codes, distance is measured from this one
name The provider’s name
street, city, state, zipcode, country The address. state may be a postal code or a full name, as the provider entered it
categories Present in the API’s records, but empty in every record seen so far
contact_telephone Phone number, as entered: formats vary
contact_website Website; may be empty
contact_others Other contact details; empty so far
languages A list column: each entry is a character vector of the languages offered, such as c("English", "Spanish")
latitude, longitude The provider’s location
distance Miles from the searched ZIP code’s location

When nothing matches, the result has all these columns and zero rows, so code that uses them still runs.

names(tidy)

Sorting and filtering

The results are ordinary tibbles, so base R or dplyr both work:

nearest <- tidy[order(tidy$distance), c("name", "street", "city", "distance")]
head(nearest)

spanish <- tidy[vapply(tidy$languages, \(x) "Spanish" %in% x, logical(1)), ]
nrow(spanish)

One row per place

As explained in vignette("services-and-searching"), a clinic that offers several services can appear once per service, each time with a different provider_id. To keep one row per place, de-duplicate on name and address:

place_key <- paste(
  tolower(tidy$name),
  tolower(tidy$street),
  tidy$zipcode
)
places <- tidy[!duplicated(place_key), ]
nrow(tidy)
nrow(places)

Names and addresses are entered by providers, so small differences in spelling or punctuation will keep two rows apart. Check the result if exact counts matter.

Saving to a file

A CSV file can’t hold a list column, so flatten languages first:

to_save <- tidy
to_save$languages <- vapply(
  to_save$languages,
  \(x) paste(x, collapse = "; "),
  character(1)
)
write.csv(to_save, "providers.csv", row.names = FALSE)

Saving as an R data file keeps the list column as it is:

saveRDS(tidy, "providers.rds")

Mapping

latitude and longitude are ordinary numbers, so any mapping package can use them. For example, with the sf and leaflet packages, which CDCLocator doesn’t need and doesn’t install for you:

providers_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(
  tidy,
  coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
  crs = 4326
)

leaflet::leaflet(providers_sf) |>
  leaflet::addTiles() |>
  leaflet::addMarkers(popup = ~name)

Keeping track of when you searched

The API’s listings change as providers open, close and update their details. If results feed into a report or analysis, record the date of the search and the arguments you used, and save the results rather than re-running the search later and expecting the same answer.
